actions.intent: Route chat requests through providers that require a deployment identifier or engine argument while preserving ordinary requests when those settings are absent.
actions.pre_state: Request dispatch sends the common chat-completion fields but cannot express provider-specific deployment or engine routing.
actions.post_state: Each request includes deployment_id and/or engine exactly when the corresponding configured client attributes exist, and otherwise retains the common request shape.
actions.validation: Mock the provider request method and assert configured routing attributes appear under the provider's expected request keys, with separate assertions that absent attributes produce no extra keys.
actions.description: Translate configured routing identifiers into the keyword arguments expected by the provider's request method, without adding absent optional fields.

actions.intent: Ensure custom requests target the endpoint belonging to the selected provider interface without allowing an environment default to override an explicit caller choice.
actions.pre_state: Client configuration may contain an explicit endpoint, either provider-specific environment endpoint may be present, and the declared authentication type identifies the active interface.
actions.post_state: At most one endpoint candidate is selected; explicit configuration wins, and an environment fallback is chosen according to the declared authentication type rather than inferred credentials.
actions.validation: Mock the external SDK constructor and assert both provider environment branches, both-environment disambiguation under an explicit authentication type, and explicit-over-environment precedence.
actions.description: Select the endpoint candidate at the provider-client boundary: retain an explicit runtime endpoint when present; otherwise read the environment slot associated with the declared authentication interface.

actions.intent: Execute a broad-write policy while keeping standard operating-system devices usable and explicit denial boundaries effective through symlinks and mount aliases.
actions.pre_state: The sandbox receives a policy containing a writable filesystem root plus explicit denied carveouts; aliases or protected metadata entries may resolve into the root or denied subtrees.
actions.post_state: The root is writable, the minimal device tree is restored, redundant root aliases and metadata remounts do not undo masks, literal and resolved denial paths are enforced, and only explicit nested writable carveouts reopen access.
actions.validation: Inspect mount-plan ordering and run sandboxed commands that access standard devices, write allowed outputs and metadata, fail on denied reads, reject writable-symlink crossings, and keep denied sibling paths inaccessible.
actions.description: Translate the broadened policy into mount operations whose ordering preserves standard devices and prevents aliases, metadata symlinks, or resolved-path handling from bypassing explicit denial masks.

actions.intent: Keep caller-visible output, subsequent conversation context, and durable history consistent across continuation success or recovery-mode replacement.
actions.module_role: conversation history and recovery lifecycle owner
actions.pre_state: Continuation state is staged and either the resumed attempt has succeeded or another recovery path is replacing it with a fresh restart.
actions.post_state: After success, durable history contains one complete model response with no duplicate overlap or synthetic recovery turn; after supersession, stale delivered text and continuation metadata are absent from both the next request and final history.
actions.validation: Assert complete history for normal, leading-thought, and thought-only completion shapes; assert invalid-stream and compression restarts omit the discarded prefix and store only the clean restarted answer.
actions.description: On success, merge the delivered prefix into the final model turn with overlap and part ordering preserved; when a fresh restart supersedes continuation, clear all staged state before resending.

actions.intent: Make every configured fallback credential available to authentication while preserving source precedence.
actions.pre_state: Credential sources have an established priority, but resolution returns a single credential and can therefore hide later fallbacks once an earlier source parses successfully.
actions.post_state: Every successfully loaded credential is represented in priority order, and failure to load one source does not prevent later configured sources from being collected.
actions.validation: Exercise valid-primary, missing-primary, invalid-source, and secondary-source cases; assert ordering and that later candidates remain reachable.
actions.description: Resolve configured credential sources into a priority-preserving candidate list while isolating source-specific read, parse, and storage failures.

actions.intent: Make future classifier drift or one-sided input/output updates observable in the unit-test suite.
actions.pre_state: No test directly specifies the official alias's expected input and output limits, allowing it to fall through silently or allowing only one capability table to be updated.
actions.post_state: A focused oracle requires the alias to return the intended input and output values, and surrounding assertions continue to constrain the generic family behavior.
actions.validation: The test passes only when the alias returns 1,000,000 for input and 384,000 for output; adjacent assertions verify representative older-family input mappings remain 131,072.
actions.description: Encode the corrected alias behavior in a focused test that checks both context-window and output-generation limits, with neighboring family tests guarding classifier precedence.

actions.intent: Prevent ambient access keys from silently overriding a deliberately selected credential profile without disabling valid access-key fallback.
actions.pre_state: A complete access-key pair is always assigned as explicit client credentials when authentication is enabled, even when an authoritative profile has been selected.
actions.post_state: Explicit client credentials are assigned only when authentication is enabled, a complete access-key pair exists, and no authoritative profile marker exists; otherwise the selected profile remains available to the SDK credential chain.
actions.validation: Inspect the mocked client constructor configuration: explicit or scoped profile plus ambient keys must omit credentials; keys without an authoritative profile must remain populated, including the ambient-profile-plus-keys case.
actions.description: Conditionally omit direct access-key credentials when an explicit or stored/scoped profile should control SDK credential resolution, while preserving access-key and skip-auth fallback behavior outside that condition.

actions.intent: Allow a context-preserving summary operation to survive temporary transport or provider failures without retrying deterministic failures indefinitely.
actions.pre_state: A summary request has returned an assistant error response, and an optional retry policy and abort signal are available.
actions.post_state: The request either succeeds within the configured retry budget, returns the final classified error without exceeding the budget, or returns an aborted response when cancellation occurs; quota-like and other non-retryable failures are not repeated.
actions.validation: Use a scripted producer to assert one call on success, abort, disabled policy, and non-retryable errors; initial-call-plus-maxRetries calls on exhaustion; early termination on recovery; ordered lifecycle callbacks; and cancellation of an in-progress backoff.
parameters: error classifier: transient versus terminal assistant error
actions.description: Wrap one assistant-producing summary request with retry classification, exponential backoff, a fixed retry budget, abort-aware waiting, and lifecycle callbacks.

actions.intent: Recover replayable state from an incomplete final record without destroying the original session if repair is interrupted.
actions.pre_state: Replay has accepted all preceding mutations and identified a parse failure confined to the final physical line with an underlying parse cause.
actions.post_state: On successful publication the session contains the valid prefix; on staging or rename failure the original bytes remain unchanged and the staging file is removed.
actions.validation: Inject a failure after damaging the staged repair file, then assert open reports a storage error, the original session bytes are unchanged, and no .tmp file remains.
actions.description: Stage the valid JSONL prefix separately and replace the damaged session only after the repaired file is complete.

actions.intent: Ensure a detector firing produces an actionable, consistently typed halt rather than allowing queued work to continue or reporting an ambiguous failure.
actions.pre_state: The always-on detector has returned true and recorded the semantic stagnation loop type while pending tool requests may exist.
actions.post_state: Pending requests are discarded, a typed loop event is emitted, the turn terminates through the existing cleanup path, telemetry can distinguish the reason, and headless output explains the halt and configuration behavior.
actions.validation: Inspect the production call site and reporting mappings to confirm the same loop type drives cleanup, stream output, telemetry, and the human-readable message.
actions.description: Carry the newly detected reason through telemetry, stream termination, pending-call cleanup, and user-facing reporting so consumers observe a consistent contract.

actions.intent: Construct a bounded summarizer request while eliminating reversal-based traversal and keeping message order explicit.
actions.pre_state: An oversized conversation has been divided into a compactable head and a preserved tail, and each message has a known token count.
actions.post_state: The selected head input is an original-order prefix whose cumulative tokens do not exceed the first summarizer model's declared or fallback capacity minus the safety reserve.
actions.validation: Use messages with distinct identities and token weights, capture the input passed to the summary operation, and assert original ordering plus cumulative size at or below the effective model-input ceiling; static diff inspection confirms the forward accumulation but the pinned suite lacks this targeted oracle.
actions.description: Choose a prefix of the compactable history head whose cumulative token count stays within the summarizer model's input capacity after a safety reserve, without reversing parallel message and size collections.

actions.intent: Determine and validate all state required by a session fork before any destination is published.
actions.pre_state: A valid source session state and fork scope, target entry, and position options are available.
actions.post_state: A consecutively sequenced mutation list represents the selected entries, resulting lanes, optional session name, and labels; an invalid fork target fails before destination publication.
actions.validation: Create and reopen branch and tree forks, then compare message counts, entries, lanes, name, labels, and excluded records with the selected source state.
actions.description: Convert fork selection options and current session state into one ordered mutation plan shared by persistent and in-memory backends.

actions.intent: Let clients select broad-root behavior only when the executor declares the required safety guarantees.
actions.pre_state: Clients cannot distinguish executors that safely preserve devices and denial restrictions during Linux root writes from executors lacking those guarantees.
actions.post_state: Executors expose two independent opt-in guarantees; absent fields deserialize as false and false values remain absent from legacy-compatible serialization.
actions.validation: Serialize default, partial, and full capability values; deserialize each supported form; and compare locally advertised values with the target platform.
actions.description: Expose independently detectable support for root-write device preservation and approved-root restriction preservation, with false values omitted for wire compatibility.

actions.intent: Prevent a supported model alias from receiving undersized context and output budgets that can trigger premature or truncated long-session compaction.
actions.module_role: Model-capability budget resolver used during runtime configuration initialization
actions.pre_state: A supported official model identifier misses the specific capability rules, selects a generic input-family fallback, and uses the default output fallback.
actions.post_state: The official identifier selects its evidence-backed input and output capability tiers before any broader family fallback, while unrelated family members retain their prior mappings.
actions.validation: Resolve the affected identifier for both input and output limit types and compare the returned values with the model's intended capability tiers; also check representative broader-family identifiers for unchanged fallback behavior.
actions.description: Extend the specific, ordered model classifiers so an official alias selects the same input-window and output-capacity tiers as its equivalent versioned family names, without altering older-family fallbacks.

actions.intent: Produce one usable persisted runtime route from layered session metadata without replacing newer or more specific route fields with a stale or non-routable fallback identity.
actions.pre_state: A session row may contain a provider-bearing nested runtime snapshot, partial top-level route fields, a routable billing provider, a bare non-routable billing bucket, malformed configuration, or combinations of these states.
actions.post_state: A provider-bearing nested runtime route wins; otherwise top-level route fields are retained and a routable billing provider fills only an absent provider; bare billing buckets and malformed metadata do not create a provider override.
actions.validation: Exercise nested precedence, partial top-level fallback, malformed metadata, routable billing fallback, bare-bucket rejection, and explicit-provider precedence through the canonical reader tests.
actions.description: Normalize layered session metadata so the canonical reader preserves explicit top-level endpoint and wire fields while filling only a missing provider from a routable historical fallback.

actions.intent: Avoid prompting for or denying trust merely because passive context exists, without exposing executable or configuration-driven project effects.
actions.pre_state: Passive instruction files and effect-bearing project resources share one trust-triggering classification and are both suppressed when untrusted.
actions.post_state: Only effect-bearing configuration and resource locations trigger trust resolution; passive context can load independently while executable and configuration resources remain gated.
actions.validation: Create an untrusted project containing both instruction files and effect-bearing resources; assert instruction context loads, effect-bearing resources do not, and instruction files alone do not satisfy the trust-input predicate.
actions.description: Define trust inputs around resources that can install packages, execute extensions, or alter runtime behavior, while allowing passive instruction files to remain available without forcing a trust decision.

actions.intent: Prevent raw structured-call argument markup from reaching visible or stored assistant text when a truncated serialization begins with a bare tool name.
actions.module_role: Malformed structured-output sanitizer shared by assistant-content consumers
actions.pre_state: A line contains a truncated argument-tag serialization whose first tag is glued to a bare identifier-like call name, and the sanitizer only recognizes tags that directly begin the line.
actions.post_state: The name-prefixed fragment is classified as unrecoverable structured output and removed, while prefixes containing prose-separating spaces remain outside this new match shape.
actions.validation: Apply the sanitizer to complete and cut name-prefixed fragments and verify that only the preceding visible text remains; also verify that spaced inline prose examples survive.
actions.description: Extend a line-oriented malformed-call detector to admit only an identifier-like prefix attached directly to an argument tag, preserving its existing line boundary and prose-safety constraints.

actions.intent: Establish a regression oracle showing that every relevant assistant-content boundary removes the newly recognized malformed fragments without broadening deletion into ordinary prose.
actions.pre_state: Multiple content sanitizers are expected to provide equivalent tool-call tag coverage, but the name-prefixed truncated-fragment shape lacks an explicit shared regression case.
actions.post_state: Both display and storage sanitizer variants are checked against complete and cut name-prefixed fragments, and preservation tests constrain false-positive removal.
actions.validation: Run the parameterized fragment test for both sanitizer variants and the adjacent prose-preservation tests; the expected outputs retain visible prefixes and remove malformed markup.
actions.description: Encode the malformed inputs and preservation expectations once, then exercise both consumer-facing sanitizers to prevent their structured-output contracts from diverging.

actions.intent: Withhold completeness when wrappers, outputs, retries, or resumed runtime handles are ambiguous or inconsistent.
actions.pre_state: Recorded calls may be attached to duplicated outputs, mismatched wrappers, reused origins, colliding direct calls, resumed waits, or retry history whose association evidence has changed.
actions.post_state: Only a unique, ordered, type-correct association can retain completeness, and once the associated inventory or mapping is invalidated all retained outputs for that runtime cell remain incomplete.
actions.validation: Recorder regressions cover mismatched wrappers, reused origins, duplicate IDs, forked waits, and retry/compaction loss; end-to-end tests cover resumed runtime-cell reuse and compaction.
actions.description: Verify that every completion-bearing output has one preceding, type-correct exec or wait input with the expected origin and runtime handle, and make any loss of that evidence irreversible for the affected cell.

actions.intent: Prevent newline insertion from bypassing the command classification that gates potentially dangerous effects.
actions.pre_state: The classifier applies dot-based dangerous-command patterns with case-insensitive matching, but dot expressions stop at newlines and may return a non-dangerous classification for split commands.
actions.post_state: The same pattern catalog is evaluated with dot matching extended across newlines, so covered dangerous constructs retain their classification when split across lines.
actions.validation: Exercise representative dot-based patterns with relevant tokens separated by newlines and require a dangerous result while retaining the existing single-line and benign-command test contract.
actions.description: Adjust the shared pattern-matching semantics so dangerous constructs remain recognizable when their relevant tokens are separated by newline characters.

actions.intent: Continue generation after visible output has been delivered without replaying the original response or persisting synthetic recovery turns.
actions.module_role: stream attempt request builder and retry-event producer
actions.pre_state: Continuation recovery has been selected and a nonblank delivered-text prefix has been accumulated.
actions.post_state: The next attempt contains a temporary model prefix and user resume instruction, the caller receives a continuation retry signal, and durable conversation history remains free of synthetic recovery turns.
actions.validation: Assert the next request's final two turns contain the delivered model prefix and resume instruction, RETRY carries isContinuation true, caller-visible chunks concatenate in order, and history contains no synthetic instruction.
actions.description: Resume an interrupted answer by adding the already delivered response and an overlap-averse resume instruction only to the next request while signaling the consumer to retain its current output buffer.

actions.intent: Keep retry timing stable while errors cross abstraction and provider boundaries.
actions.pre_state: A lower-layer error contains a captured retry deadline and must be translated, reclassified, reworded, or retained after a retry budget is exhausted.
actions.post_state: The translated or retained error exposes the identical original deadline; its remaining duration decreases with elapsed time and reaches zero without becoming absent.
actions.validation: Map errors after virtual time advances and assert deadline identity, decreasing remaining delay, zero-after-expiry behavior, and preservation through provider-specific rewriting and exhausted retry state.
actions.description: Carry the same captured deadline through transport, API, provider, protocol, and exhausted-retry representations even when the semantic error type or user-facing message changes.

actions.intent: Prevent cold HTTP load and resume operations from reading or continuing session state under a process-default runtime root when a different workspace runtime was selected.
actions.pre_state: A restore request has selected a workspace runtime whose sessionRuntimeBaseDir may differ from the ambient Storage runtime base directory, while the archive-coordinated asynchronous restore operation is still invoked without an ambient runtime binding.
actions.post_state: The archive-coordinated restore, persisted-session resolution, metadata reads, and selected bridge load/resume call execute with the ambient Storage runtime base directory equal to the selected workspace runtime’s sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
actions.validation: For both load and resume, persist the target session under a secondary runtime root, invoke the HTTP restore route for that workspace, assert success, and assert the selected bridge observes that secondary root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir().
actions.description: Bind the full asynchronous HTTP load/resume critical section—not only its SessionService instance—to the selected workspace runtime’s storage root so nested restoration code observes the correct persisted state.

actions.intent: Preserve all unique response fragments across multiple interrupted continuation attempts without duplicating replayed text.
actions.pre_state: A continuation or initial attempt has ended in a cut after delivering zero or more text chunks, and an earlier accumulated prefix may exist.
actions.post_state: The accumulated prefix contains the unique ordered response produced through the failed attempt, and the per-attempt buffer is empty for the next attempt.
actions.validation: Simulate an intermediate continuation that repeats the previous tail and is cut again; assert the following request and durable history contain each fragment exactly once.
actions.description: Fold each failed attempt's visible text into the running prefix at the attempt boundary, removing any tail replay before that prefix is reused.

actions.intent: Authenticate with the highest-priority usable credential instead of forcing reauthentication when a higher-priority cached credential is expired, revoked, or incompatible.
actions.pre_state: An ordered set of credential candidates exists, but one candidate may fail token acquisition or server-side token validation.
actions.post_state: The first candidate that successfully produces a usable token is returned; a failed candidate is logged and does not block verification of the next candidate.
actions.validation: Make the first candidate fail token acquisition or token-info validation and make the next candidate succeed; assert that the succeeding credential is applied and returned through the public client-acquisition boundary.
actions.description: Attempt each credential candidate with its appropriate authentication client, accepting the first verified candidate and treating an individual rejection as a recoverable fallback condition.

actions.intent: Allow a resumed operation to extend prior state and return the extended state without changing the caller-owned input sequence.
actions.pre_state: A caller may supply a non-empty mutable sequence of prior messages, and the continuation routine will append new-turn messages to its working sequence.
actions.post_state: The continuation routine's outer working sequence is distinct from the supplied sequence; new-turn appends appear in the returned sequence but not in the caller's input list.
actions.validation: Provide a non-empty history, execute a completed new turn, then verify that the input sequence retains its original length while the returned sequence contains additional messages.
actions.description: Create a distinct working sequence at the continuation boundary so additions for the new turn do not alter the caller's historical-state container.

actions.intent: Allow a streamed operation interrupted by a recognized premature-close transport error to recover through the existing retry mechanism instead of terminating immediately.
actions.module_role: Shared transient-network-failure classifier used by retry execution and retry telemetry
actions.pre_state: A streaming attempt has failed with an error carrying code ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE, but that code is absent from the exact retryable network-code set.
actions.post_state: The existing network-error predicate recognizes ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as retryable, and retry telemetry preserves that code as the failure type.
actions.validation: Simulate a stream that emits partial content and throws the coded error, then provide a successful subsequent stream; require a retry event, completed response content, and telemetry labeled with the exact error code.
actions.description: Admit a specific premature-stream-termination code to an existing bounded network-error retry policy so interrupted streaming requests can use the established retry and telemetry path.

actions.intent: Ensure requests reach the adapter that implements the actual endpoint contract while avoiding false routing for similarly named or hostile hosts.
actions.pre_state: A configured OpenAI-compatible base URL would otherwise fall through to the generic provider, and the served model name is not sufficient evidence of the endpoint implementation.
actions.post_state: The canonical endpoint hostname and its subdomains select the dedicated adapter; unrelated, malformed, and suffix-confusable hosts do not.
actions.validation: Exercise canonical-host, subdomain, hostile-suffix, and unrelated-host cases and assert the resulting request behavior identifies the selected provider path.
actions.description: Recognize an endpoint using parsed hostname boundaries and route matching requests to its dedicated compatibility adapter without relying on model-family names or substring matches.

actions.intent: Keep endpoint routing and SDK provider mode consistent at the external-provider interface even when optional configuration fields were not populated upstream.
actions.pre_state: Endpoint resolution and admission have completed, while the SDK provider-mode field may be explicitly set or absent despite a declared authentication type.
actions.post_state: The SDK receives the accepted endpoint in its HTTP options and a concrete provider-mode value that preserves an explicit setting or otherwise reflects the declared authentication interface.
actions.validation: Inspect the mocked SDK constructor for endpoint forwarding and correct true/false provider-mode values, including the branch with declared cloud authentication but no inferred credentials and established non-cloud scenarios.
actions.description: Construct the provider SDK options with the validated endpoint and a concrete provider-mode flag, deriving the mode from the declared authentication interface when upstream credential inference left it unset.

actions.intent: Prevent server-requested retry timing from being restarted or lengthened by subsequent processing.
actions.pre_state: An unsuccessful response has arrived with optional raw retry-advice headers or an equivalent streamed delay signal.
actions.post_state: Valid advice is represented by one monotonic deadline captured at receipt; expired or zero advice remains present with zero remaining delay, while invalid or absent advice produces no deadline.
actions.validation: Use paused-time parser tests to verify delta-seconds countdown, HTTP-date conversion, zero and expired values, and rejection of malformed or overflowing values.
actions.description: Normalize valid relative-seconds or HTTP-date retry advice at receipt time into one monotonic deadline, while preserving the distinction between missing, invalid, expired, and explicit-zero advice.

actions.intent: Prevent an authentication method accepted at one startup boundary from being rejected at another.
actions.pre_state: Multiple startup gates independently treat absence of an API key as a credential failure.
actions.post_state: Each gate accepts a missing key only under the shared keyless eligibility contract and continues to reject missing credentials otherwise.
actions.validation: Run focused CLI and core validation cases for eligible keyless configuration, missing project, strict validation, explicit key-variable configuration, and unrelated auth modes.
actions.description: Make CLI preflight and core configuration validation accept the same eligible project-only state while retaining errors for all excluded states.

actions.intent: Resume a prior conversation automatically without overwriting authoritative in-memory state supplied by the current caller.
actions.pre_state: A new session has either explicit completed-message state, or an empty completed-message state plus an optional configured persisted transcript.
actions.post_state: Explicit state remains authoritative; otherwise a nonempty persisted transcript becomes the session's completed-message state, and restored state is announced when present.
actions.validation: Initialize once with explicit completed messages and once with an empty state plus a populated transcript; verify the first state is unchanged, the second contains reconstructed history, and the restoration announcement appears only for nonempty completed state. These branches are present in the pinned code but lack an automated regression test.
actions.description: At lifecycle initialization, preserve caller-provided completed messages; otherwise load and reconstruct the configured transcript and expose restoration to the user.

actions.intent: Choose a recovery mode that preserves already observed output while avoiding invalid structured-call sequences and unbounded retries.
actions.pre_state: A streaming attempt ended with a classified retryable transport error, with per-send accumulated visible text and per-attempt structured-call observations available.
actions.post_state: Exactly one applicable outcome is selected: replay when no nonblank visible text has accumulated and replay budget remains; continue when visible text exists, no function call was emitted, and continuation budget remains; otherwise propagate the error.
actions.validation: Exercise text, blank-text, thought-only, function-call, repeated-cut, and exhausted-budget cases; assert request shape, retry-event mode, attempt count, and final error behavior.
actions.description: Classify a retryable stream cut using accumulated caller-visible output, structured-call state, and separate recovery budgets so a request is replayed only when doing so cannot duplicate or discard visible answer text.

actions.intent: Keep each serialized tool result unambiguously correlated with the tool call that produced it.
actions.module_role: Conversation-history adapter at the structured tool-call boundary
actions.pre_state: Internal assistant tool calls and tool results contain matching identifiers, but serialization omits both identifiers because the capability predicate is false.
actions.post_state: For protocols classified as requiring IDs, each serialized function call and corresponding function response carries the same normalized identifier; protocols outside that class retain the prior omission behavior.
actions.validation: Serialize histories containing multiple calls and matching results, assert ordered ID equality on both sides for each supported adapter, and assert IDs remain absent for an older protocol version.
actions.description: Use the shared capability decision to serialize the same correlated identifier on both the function call and its response while retaining omission for protocols that do not require it.

actions.intent: Correct conflicting-credential selection without breaking configurations that rely on a generic compatible credential because no endpoint-specific credential is configured.
actions.pre_state: The endpoint-specific credential is absent while a generic credential accepted by the selected compatible endpoint is present.
actions.post_state: The resolver returns the generic compatible credential after exhausting the explicit and endpoint-specific slots.
actions.validation: Run the fallback regression test with OPENROUTER_API_KEY removed and OPENAI_API_KEY set; it asserts the returned api_key equals the generic fallback value.
actions.description: Guard the precedence correction with an oracle proving that installations which only provide the generic OpenAI-compatible credential continue to resolve a usable key.

actions.intent: Permit an ambient credential resolver only when routing context is present and no explicit secret contract would be bypassed.
actions.pre_state: A selected provider configuration has no resolved API key and may or may not declare its own key variable or contain a usable project identifier.
actions.post_state: The configuration is classified as keyless-eligible only for the supported auth mode, with no declared key variable and a nonblank project identifier.
actions.validation: Exercise project-present, project-absent, whitespace-only, alternate-auth-type, and explicit-key-variable cases; only the eligible project-only cases may pass.
actions.description: Determine whether the selected authentication mode may use ambient default credentials without overriding a provider entry that explicitly declares a key source.

actions.intent: Bound a loop whose tool arguments vary while its observable read-only operation remains unchanged.
actions.pre_state: No loop has fired, detection is enabled for the session, and incoming tool requests may repeatedly map to the same semantic inspection key.
actions.post_state: At the threshold the loop is marked detected with a dedicated reason and logged; before the threshold processing continues, while nonmatching calls, retries, and prompt resets clear the streak.
actions.validation: Verify no detection through threshold minus one, detection and telemetry at the threshold, streak restart after nonmatching calls and retries, and suppression after session disable.
actions.description: Track consecutive requests sharing the semantic inspection key, reset on progress or replay boundaries, and halt at the bounded threshold while respecting the explicit session override.

actions.intent: Prevent an automatic-approval mode from bypassing argument-level policy constraints when effect arguments cannot be parsed reliably.
actions.module_role: effect authorization boundary that reconciles parser confidence with matched policy restrictions
actions.pre_state: An effect request is being evaluated in automatic-approval mode; a matched rule would allow it but carries an argument restriction, and parsing yields either no usable command details or an error-bearing result.
actions.post_state: The request is denied whenever argument-restricted authorization cannot be validated from reliable parse output; explicit denials remain denied, while unrestricted automatic approvals remain eligible for ALLOW.
actions.validation: Mock both empty/error and nonempty/error parser results for a request matching an argument-restricted ALLOW rule and assert DENY; retain adjacent tests proving default unrestricted YOLO ALLOW and explicit DENY behavior.
parameters: effect request and raw argument string
actions.description: At an automatic-approval boundary, classify empty or error-bearing parser output as unreliable and deny an otherwise allowed effect when the matched policy depends on argument-level restrictions that can no longer be validated, while preserving behavior for explicit denials and unrestricted approvals.

actions.intent: Prevent invalid or insecure remote endpoint overrides from reaching the provider SDK while preserving local development connectivity.
actions.pre_state: A non-empty explicit or environment-derived custom endpoint has been selected but has not yet been admitted to outbound client options.
actions.post_state: The endpoint is admitted only if it is parseable and uses HTTPS, except that named and numeric loopback hosts may use HTTP; rejected values fail before SDK construction.
actions.validation: Assert acceptance of an HTTP loopback URL and rejection of both an unparsable string and an HTTP remote URL with the expected error classes/messages.
actions.description: Parse any selected custom endpoint and enforce encrypted transport for remote hosts while retaining an HTTP exception for local loopback development.

actions.intent: Ensure every resume interface restores the provider, endpoint, and protocol belonging to the session's latest persisted runtime route.
actions.pre_state: The resume adapter independently reads only top-level route fields and billing metadata, while another execution path persists the latest route in a nested runtime snapshot and another resume consumer already uses the canonical resolver.
actions.post_state: The resume adapter obtains provider, endpoint, and API mode through the canonical resolver, then applies its existing endpoint-ownership checks, provider healing, and override construction.
actions.validation: Assert that resume selects nested runtime data over a stale first-call billing provider and over stale top-level route keys, and compare the restored route with the existing CLI resume consumer.
actions.description: Adapt a resume interface that had its own incomplete metadata reader to consume the canonical route resolver, while leaving its interface-specific override construction and safety repairs intact.

actions.intent: Route requests to the intended cloud endpoint without converting a keyless configuration into a conflicting key-based mode.
actions.pre_state: Client construction may depend on an earlier environment mutation, and a placeholder or empty key can alter SDK authentication semantics.
actions.post_state: The selected cloud auth type produces explicit cloud mode with no API key supplied; other auth types retain SDK environment fallback unless explicitly configured.
actions.validation: Construct the client with the cloud auth type, a configured project, no mode-selection environment value, and no API key; assert cloud mode is true and the key is undefined.
actions.description: Select the cloud endpoint directly from the resolved auth type and preserve an absent API key so the SDK can resolve ambient credentials.

actions.intent: Prevent a single transient stream drop from aborting context compaction or branch preservation while keeping extension-supplied summaries outside the model retry path.
actions.pre_state: Context compaction or branch navigation requires a generated model summary, but summary call paths either invoke the provider once or do not receive the runtime retry policy.
actions.post_state: Every model-generated history, split-turn prefix, and branch summary runs through the bounded retry helper with the operation's existing abort signal and configured retry settings; summaries supplied by hooks or extensions remain direct inputs.
actions.validation: Script transient errors followed by success at manual/automatic compaction and branch-summary entry points, then assert the operation completes with the recovered summary; separately assert deterministic failure, disabled policy, exhaustion, and abort behavior.
actions.description: Propagate the existing retry configuration, cancellation signal, and callbacks through manual compaction, automatic compaction, split-turn prefix summarization, and branch summarization so all generated context summaries share the same resilience boundary.

actions.intent: Prevent regression to input-list aliasing while confirming that conversation continuation still records the new turn.
actions.pre_state: A continuation API accepts an existing mutable history and returns a message history after processing another turn.
actions.post_state: The regression oracle demonstrates that the supplied history's outer length is unchanged and the returned history is longer than the original.
actions.validation: Use a deterministic mocked completion, suppress persistence and cleanup side effects, call the continuation API, assert input length equality with the saved baseline, and assert returned length exceeds that baseline.
actions.description: Exercise the continuation boundary with controlled side effects and check both halves of the ownership contract: unchanged caller state and an independently extended result.

actions.intent: Make a prepared file become visible as one replacement event without exposing intermediate destination content.
actions.pre_state: A complete source file and a destination path on a filesystem that supports same-filesystem atomic rename are available.
actions.post_state: On success the source no longer exists and the destination contains the source content; on rename failure the existing destination remains unchanged and the error identifies the failing source when available.
actions.validation: Replace an existing destination and assert the source disappears and new content is visible; inject a missing-source failure and assert the prior destination content remains.
actions.description: Expose a filesystem operation that commits a fully prepared sibling file by atomically replacing the destination and returns structured path-aware failures.

actions.intent: Avoid silently changing the authenticated principal after a configured secret fails to resolve.
actions.pre_state: A provider entry declares a key variable, the variable is unset, and ambient credentials might otherwise be available.
actions.post_state: Validation continues to fail on the declared key variable and does not offer or activate the ambient credential path.
actions.validation: Configure a declared key variable plus a project while leaving the variable unset; assert validation fails on that variable in both CLI and core and omits the keyless hint.
actions.description: Keep a declared secret source mandatory instead of silently authenticating through ambient credentials when that secret is missing.

actions.intent: Prevent a configured shell-output allowance from exceeding the estimated context capacity left after the latest prompt while preserving stricter configured limits.
actions.pre_state: The output-budget provider returns a static configured character threshold even though model context capacity and the latest prompt token count are available.
actions.post_state: The provided character threshold is the minimum of the configured ceiling and the estimated remaining token capacity converted at four characters per token.
actions.validation: Mock the model token limit and latest prompt usage, then assert both minimum-selection branches for default and custom configured ceilings.
actions.description: Derive the output-character threshold from both the configured ceiling and an estimate of remaining model capacity, selecting the smaller value before the existing truncation call site consumes it.

actions.intent: Prevent denied project configuration from causing package installation, code execution, runtime resource injection, or local settings mutation.
actions.pre_state: A command is about to resolve project settings, install packages, load executable resources, or write project-local package configuration without a uniformly installed authorization result.
actions.post_state: Denied projects contribute no gated resources or package-install effects and cannot receive local package-setting writes; authorized projects are reloaded and processed normally.
actions.validation: For an untrusted project, assert project extensions, skills, prompts, themes, system prompt, and package installation output are absent and local configuration mutation is rejected; separately verify authorized package listing succeeds.
actions.description: Apply the resolved trust state to settings and resource resolution before loading project packages or resources, and reject project-local configuration writes when authorization is false.

actions.intent: Identify when a profile represents a deliberate request or stored authentication choice that must outrank ambient access keys.
actions.module_role: Credential-source precedence resolver at the provider client boundary
actions.pre_state: Profile lookup collapses explicit, stored/scoped, and ambient profile sources into one client field, so later credential injection cannot tell whether the profile is authoritative.
actions.post_state: An authoritative-profile marker is present only for an explicit option or scoped request environment; the client may still receive an ambient profile through the fallback lookup without marking it authoritative.
actions.validation: Capture client configuration for explicit, scoped, and ambient-only profiles; explicit and scoped inputs must be recognized as precedence-bearing, while ambient-only profile discovery must retain the distinct behavior demonstrated by the access-key fallback test.
actions.description: Derive a profile marker only from request-explicit or stored/scoped configuration, while retaining ambient profile discovery solely as the client profile fallback. This preserves source provenance for the later credential-precedence decision.

actions.intent: Prevent authentication failures caused by sending a credential for one service to a different selected endpoint when multiple compatible credential variables coexist.
actions.module_role: Credential precedence policy shared by eager client state and runtime provider resolution
actions.pre_state: The selected runtime is OpenRouter-compatible, no explicit credential overrides the environment, and both endpoint-specific and generic compatible credentials may be present; existing paths prioritize the generic credential inconsistently with the selected endpoint.
actions.post_state: All inspected resolution paths use the invariant explicit credential > endpoint-specific credential > generic compatible fallback, so the selected endpoint receives its own credential when available.
actions.validation: Compare the first-parent diff for both resolution paths and use the preferred-key regression test to prove the shared runtime resolver returns the endpoint-specific credential when both environment variables are populated.
actions.description: Reconcile every credential-resolution path so an explicitly supplied credential remains strongest, the credential dedicated to the selected endpoint wins over a generic compatible credential, and the generic credential remains a fallback.

actions.intent: Avoid presenting project configuration as proof of a usable authentication token.
actions.pre_state: No API key is observed, but the configuration is eligible to attempt ambient credential resolution at session start.
actions.post_state: Preflight reports an indeterminate authentication state with no confirmed token and defers credential proof to session startup.
actions.validation: Request preflight status for an eligible keyless configuration and assert unknown status, unknown token presence, and no immediate missing-key error.
actions.description: Represent routing readiness separately from proof that an ambient credential can actually resolve.

actions.intent: Produce one consistent authorization result for every execution surface and deny unresolved effect-bearing projects in non-interactive contexts.
actions.pre_state: Runtime and administrative commands may apply different trust rules, and no single precedence contract covers overrides, hooks, stored decisions, defaults, and UI availability.
actions.post_state: All callers receive a boolean decision from the same precedence order, with persisted decisions overriding defaults and missing UI or cancelled prompts resolving to denial.
actions.validation: Exercise explicit overrides, no-input projects, extension results, stored false over default always, valid and invalid global defaults, interactive selection, and headless fallback.
actions.description: Centralize trust resolution with explicit precedence across command overrides, absence of gated inputs, policy hooks, persisted decisions, global defaults, and interactive confirmation.

actions.intent: Allow extensible trust decisions without executing the untrusted project's own code during the decision process.
actions.pre_state: Trust has not been resolved, but extension hooks may participate in the decision and normal loading could include project-local effects.
actions.post_state: Decision hooks from non-project sources are available while project settings, packages, and extensions remain excluded until authorization completes.
actions.validation: Provide a non-project project_trust hook and project package settings; verify the hook can authorize access and that the bootstrap loader begins with projectTrusted false.
actions.description: Run a restricted bootstrap pass with project trust disabled so globally supplied or explicit hooks may decide trust before project-local packages and extensions become eligible.

actions.intent: Honor upstream timing without changing retry eligibility, retry budgets, fallback behavior, or the no-advice backoff policy.
actions.pre_state: A failure is independently classified as retryable, retry budget remains, and the error may or may not contain a server deadline.
actions.post_state: Advice-bearing retries resume no earlier than the original deadline despite propagation or notification time; retries without advice use local backoff; terminal errors and exhausted budgets remain terminal under existing policy.
actions.validation: Verify end-to-end HTTP recovery and request count, paused-time fallback backoff, delayed stream notification against the original deadline, and retained advice after HTTP retry exhaustion.
actions.description: For retryable failures within budget, wait until the server's absolute deadline when present and otherwise retain the established local-backoff policy; compute telemetry from the remaining wait after intervening work.

actions.intent: Recover a live turn that repeatedly produces no usable answer instead of terminating it as an incomplete partial result before a fallback is tried.
actions.pre_state: The consecutive no-answer response threshold has been reached during an incomplete turn, and a configured fallback may be available; the triggering response may have consumed the remaining iteration budget.
actions.post_state: If fallback activation succeeds, recovery counters are reset, the same turn continues under the fallback identity, and at most one budget-grace call permits the fallback request. If no fallback is available, the existing terminal partial-result path remains in force.
actions.validation: Supply three consecutive reasoning-only responses at a three-call budget followed by a successful fallback response; assert the typed failover reason, completed answer, exactly four calls, and a consumed grace flag.
actions.description: After the configured consecutive-stall threshold, activate the existing fallback chain with a typed failure reason and reserve one call when the ordinary turn budget has already been consumed.

actions.intent: Distinguish a persistent nonproductive response loop from ordinary incomplete responses that make visible progress.
actions.pre_state: The turn receives an incomplete response and already maintains aggregate continuation accounting, but consecutive responses with no visible answer or tool call are not independently represented.
actions.post_state: Each incomplete response has updated consecutive-stall state: a no-answer/no-tool response increments the streak, while observable progress resets it; the state is reset at normal completion and turn boundaries.
actions.validation: Drive a visible partial followed by three reasoning-only incomplete responses and verify that failover occurs only after the three consecutive nonproductive responses.
actions.description: Track a local consecutive streak for incomplete responses that contain neither visible answer text nor a tool call, resetting it when observable progress occurs so nonconsecutive failures do not trigger recovery.

actions.intent: Keep unrelated complete tool-call inventories trustworthy when another output exceeds the metadata budget.
actions.pre_state: Serialized tool-call metadata exceeds argument, per-output, or request limits, so some evidence must be truncated or omitted.
actions.post_state: Optional result metadata and sources are shed first; an over-budget output carries its own omission marker; completion is cleared for every output sharing the damaged cell but remains available to intact unrelated cells.
actions.validation: Protocol tests exercise budget priority and fail-closed completion, recorder tests preserve an unrelated complete exec under overflow, and an end-to-end Code Mode test verifies the same behavior.
actions.description: Apply request-size limits per output, preserve stronger evidence before optional metadata, and revoke completion only where truncation or omission damaged the recorded inventory.

actions.intent: Keep metadata recording aligned with current runtime policy without altering which tools can execute or falsely certifying calls made before recording began.
actions.pre_state: A session's recording rollout may change after construction, or a legacy reload may carry the session's original feature snapshot rather than current host policy.
actions.post_state: Normal runtime refresh atomically creates or removes recorder state without changing execution gates; late-created state marks prior history unobserved, and legacy reload preserves the existing recorder.
actions.validation: Recorder and end-to-end tests verify runtime enablement, absence of completeness when earlier history was unobserved, and preservation of prepared call bindings across refresh.
actions.description: Allow runtime rollout configuration to enable or disable evidence recording independently from tool dispatch, while preventing stale legacy snapshots from replacing a valid live recorder.

actions.intent: Identify histories whose external structured-tool protocol requires explicit correlation identifiers.
actions.module_role: Protocol capability classifier shared by message serialization
actions.pre_state: The classifier recognizes existing model families but returns false for a newer protocol generation whose tool interactions require explicit IDs.
actions.post_state: The classifier returns true for the newer major-version boundary and existing required families, and false for the verified older version.
actions.validation: Evaluate representative identifiers immediately below and above the version boundary plus existing true cases; expect Gemini 2.5 false and Gemini 3.6, Claude, and GPT-OSS true.
parameters: minimum major version requiring explicit IDs
actions.description: Extend the shared capability predicate at the version boundary while preserving existing model-family behavior and excluding older versions.

actions.intent: Recover reusable conversational state from a human-readable persisted transcript without replaying operational noise as dialogue.
actions.pre_state: A configured transcript contains interleaved session headings, user headings, assistant text, commands, and blockquoted operational output.
actions.post_state: The transcript is represented as an ordered list of user and assistant message objects, with recognized non-conversational records excluded.
actions.validation: Use a transcript containing each supported record type and verify that ordinary user headings and intervening assistant text are emitted in order while session headings, blockquotes, slash commands, and <blank> prompts are absent. The pinned implementation directly establishes these parsing rules, but the change supplies no automated test oracle.
actions.description: Convert the application's append-only Markdown transcript into model-facing user and assistant messages while excluding session metadata, tool output, commands, and empty prompts.

actions.intent: Prevent identifier reuse or unavailable history from producing a false tool-call completion claim.
actions.pre_state: A recorder may encounter call origins or runtime handles that were already present in initial history, reused during the session, or unavailable because historical indexing exceeded a safety bound.
actions.post_state: Completion can begin only for identifiers proven fresh against bounded historical and live observations; collisions, oversized identifiers, and incomplete history indexing fail closed.
actions.validation: Bounded-filter tests verify namespace separation and saturation behavior; recorder tests verify that paginated known IDs and reused origins are rejected while genuinely fresh origins remain usable.
actions.description: Maintain bounded, monotonic knowledge of historical and live identifiers so reused or unindexable identifiers cannot be treated as fresh evidence for completion.

actions.intent: Recognize repeated operations that are semantically equivalent despite argument variation without misclassifying productive shell work.
actions.pre_state: A shell tool request contains an unclassified command string that may have multiple chained segments.
actions.post_state: The request has either one stable overview-inspection key or no stagnation key; write-bearing, mixed-purpose, non-repository, and path-specific review commands have no key.
actions.validation: Feed positive command variants and negative boundary cases through the always-on checker; only complete chains of overview-style read-only inspections may contribute to the common streak.
actions.description: Normalize syntactically varied shell requests into one stagnation class only when every command segment performs repository-wide read-only inspection, while treating productive or narrowly targeted commands as progress.

actions.intent: Keep resumed state usable when persisted history is larger than either the desired conversation budget or the summarizer model's request context.
actions.pre_state: Reconstructed completed messages may exceed the configured history budget, and the portion selected for summarization may exceed the summarizer model's maximum input context.
actions.post_state: History within the configured budget is left intact; oversized history starts compaction, and the summarizer receives the newest portion of the selected head that fits its input limit with a reserve.
actions.validation: Exercise histories below and above the configured budget and use a model with a known max_input_tokens value; verify no worker starts below the threshold, a worker starts above it, and the messages passed to summarization do not exceed max_input_tokens minus 512 according to the implementation's token counter. No such automated test was included in the change.
actions.description: Apply a configurable retained-history budget and bound each summarizer request to the summarizer model's input capacity before background compaction.

actions.intent: Make future changes detect regressions that reopen newline-based bypasses of the approval boundary.
actions.pre_state: The test suite covers dangerous command detection but has no explicit oracle for tokens separated by embedded newlines.
actions.post_state: The regression suite explicitly requires remote-content piping, disk-copy, and recursive-permission examples containing newlines to be classified as dangerous.
actions.validation: Run the detector test module and require all four multiline cases, together with the pre-existing classification tests, to pass.
actions.description: Encode representative newline-based bypasses as regression tests for the shared classifier.

actions.intent: Support reusable authorization for a directory tree while retaining explicit, closer overrides and a way to resume inheritance.
actions.pre_state: Persisted decisions apply only to an exact working directory, requiring duplicate entries and providing no inherited source metadata.
actions.post_state: The nearest saved ancestor decision governs each descendant unless a closer decision exists; deleting the closer entry restores inheritance, and the effective source path is observable.
actions.validation: Store a parent true decision, add a child false decision, query descendants, delete the child decision, and assert each effective value and source path.
parameters: nullable update used to delete an override
actions.description: Resolve persisted decisions hierarchically and update parent and child entries atomically so a parent policy can cover descendants without masking a closer exception.

actions.intent: Prevent protocol-specific recovery artifacts from leaking into a fallback request that cannot interpret them.
actions.module_role: Outbound conversation projection and protocol adapter
actions.pre_state: Fallback activation changes the request protocol while stored session history contains thinking-only replay rows and a synthetic continuation marker used by the prior protocol.
actions.post_state: The outbound fallback request excludes the incompatible marker and replay state, adjacent user rows are reconciled to preserve role alternation, and canonical stored session history remains available unchanged.
actions.validation: Capture the fallback wire request after a three-response stall and assert absence of the marker and opaque reasoning items plus alternating non-system roles.
actions.description: Build the fallback request from a copy of conversation history that excludes the prior protocol's synthetic continuation instruction and opaque reasoning replay state while restoring valid role alternation.

actions.intent: Make delayed or repeated context-summary requests visible to harness subscribers, external integrations, and the interactive user interface.
actions.pre_state: A generated summary request may enter backoff and retry, but consumers only observe the surrounding compaction or navigation operation.
actions.post_state: Consumers receive scheduled, attempt-start, and finished lifecycle events with retry counts, delays, errors, and operation context; the interactive interface transitions between retry and underlying operation indicators.
actions.validation: Subscribe to lifecycle events and assert scheduled/start/finished ordering and operation labels during recovery and exhaustion; verify no retry events for deterministic errors; exercise UI event branches for retry countdown, operation restoration, and cleanup.
actions.description: Translate retry callbacks into typed operation-aware events and update the interactive status so retries are observable and cancellable operations do not appear stalled.

actions.intent: Prevent ACP load and resume operations from restoring session state under a stale or default storage root after workspace-runtime selection or replacement.
actions.pre_state: An ACP restore request has resolved a sessionRuntime with its own sessionRuntimeBaseDir, but the asynchronous archive-coordinated restore callback is invoked outside that runtime’s ambient Storage context.
actions.post_state: Persisted-session lookup, metadata recovery, and the selected runtime bridge’s load/resume operation execute while Storage resolves paths from sessionRuntime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
actions.validation: For both protocol load and resume, activate a replacement runtime with a distinct storage root, store the session there, issue the request, and assert no protocol error, one restore call, and observation of the replacement root inside the bridge callback.
actions.description: Bind the complete asynchronous ACP load/resume critical section to the selected or replacement workspace runtime so bridge restoration and nested storage access remain aligned with runtime selection.

actions.intent: Prevent a compaction result from being accepted based on a token calculation that omits the context being preserved.
actions.pre_state: A head summary has been produced, a tail is being preserved verbatim, and the full tokenized-message sequence remains available.
actions.post_state: The summary-tail result is returned only when its combined token count is below the configured history budget; otherwise the combined result re-enters bounded compaction.
actions.validation: Construct a case where the summary alone fits but summary plus tail does not, then assert that recursive compaction occurs; construct a combined-fit case and assert direct return. The corrected slice is directly visible in the diff, but no targeted pinned test supplies this behavioral oracle.
actions.description: Measure the generated summary together with the untouched tail and recurse when their combined size still exceeds the configured history budget.

actions.intent: Prevent provider-specific credentials and endpoint defaults from leaking into the constructor contract of the component that manages editing behavior.
actions.pre_state: Every direct component construction requires an API key and optionally a base URL, and construction mutates the global provider client.
actions.post_state: The component constructor requires only its domain inputs and no longer mutates provider configuration; direct call sites conform to that contract.
actions.validation: Instantiate the component through the updated production and test call sites without provider credential arguments and run the existing constructor-dependent regression tests.
actions.description: Make domain-component creation independent of provider initialization after configuration ownership moves to the application boundary, then reconcile all direct construction call sites.

actions.intent: Direct users toward a valid recovery path without encouraging placeholder credentials or impossible fallbacks.
actions.pre_state: Credential validation fails and the error formatter knows the auth type and whether a key variable was explicitly declared.
actions.post_state: Eligible keyless configurations mention the project-based alternative; unrelated auth types and explicit-key-variable entries do not.
actions.validation: Assert project guidance appears for eligible missing-credential errors in normal and strict modes and is absent for unrelated auth types and explicit-key-variable entries.
actions.description: Tell users about ambient credentials when that path can work, while retaining precise key-source errors for excluded configurations.

actions.intent: Prevent strict endpoints from rejecting replayed structured messages while retaining the information they accept and preserving caller-authored values.
actions.pre_state: Shared request construction has produced assistant messages where a derived field may equal its source field, but the selected endpoint rejects the derived field during multi-turn replay.
actions.post_state: Outbound assistant messages omit the derived field only when it is the recognizable string copy of the source field; the source field, distinct explicit values, non-assistant messages, and original history remain intact.
actions.validation: Assert field-level behavior for equal and distinct values and run a multi-turn generator request against a strict endpoint that rejects the incompatible field, inspecting the accepted wire body.
actions.description: At the outbound boundary, recognize the exact compatibility field synthesized by shared request construction and remove that copy without altering source history or legitimate fields.

actions.intent: Permit an explicitly approved command to write broadly without allowing it to read paths or globs that the original policy explicitly denied.
actions.pre_state: A command has a filesystem policy and execution context; approval requires broader writes, while explicit denial entries may contain concrete, workspace-relative, or glob paths.
actions.post_state: A restricted root-write policy retains materializable explicit read denials and grants only non-denied protected metadata writes; unsafe or unresolved cases retain the original policy unchanged.
actions.validation: Compare resolved access and deny matching across Unix, drive-letter, UNC, project-root, glob, metadata, and multi-volume cases; assert conservative identity fallback for root-level or unresolved denials.
actions.description: Construct the least restrictive approved-command policy needed for broad writes, retain explicit read-denial invariants, discard unrelated old grants, and fail closed to the original policy when denials cannot be safely resolved.

actions.intent: Establish a regression oracle for the precedence between dynamic remaining capacity and the pre-existing configured threshold.
actions.pre_state: The threshold policy lacks focused examples demonstrating which bound wins under default and custom configurations.
actions.post_state: Tests encode expected results for a smaller remaining-context bound, a smaller default bound, and both precedence branches for a custom bound.
actions.validation: Run the core configuration unit tests and require the expected thresholds 124000, 4000000, 24000, and 50000 for the corresponding mocked inputs.
actions.description: Exercise the threshold policy with controlled capacity and usage values to prove that remaining context wins when smaller and the configured ceiling wins otherwise, including custom configuration.

actions.intent: Allow a compatible provider endpoint to receive its required client configuration without embedding that configuration in the domain component constructor.
actions.module_role: application composition and provider-client configuration boundary
actions.pre_state: The application accepts only key and base settings, while the domain component constructor owns provider-module initialization and forces a default base value.
actions.post_state: The application boundary accepts the supported optional provider settings and initializes the shared provider client before constructing downstream components; omitted optional settings are not overwritten.
actions.validation: Parse representative provider arguments or configuration fields and verify the corresponding provider-client attributes are set before domain-component construction, while omitted values remain untouched.
actions.description: Expose the provider's optional connection and routing settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared client before downstream components are created.

actions.intent: Prevent incomplete derived sessions from becoming discoverable after interrupted or failed fork creation.
actions.pre_state: A destination header, destination path, and complete validated fork mutation plan exist while the final destination is not yet published.
actions.post_state: Either a complete reopenable fork is present at the destination, or no fork and no staging file is visible after a reported failure.
actions.validation: Inject failures during mutation staging and final rename and assert the fork is absent from repository listing with no .tmp residue; on success reopen and verify all selected state.
actions.description: Build the fork header and all planned mutations in a sibling temporary file, then expose the fork through one atomic replacement and clean up failed staging artifacts.

workflows.name: isolate-project-effects-behind-layered-authorization
workflows.title: Resolve project authorization before activating local effects
workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for separating passive context from effect-bearing project inputs, safely loading non-project policy hooks, resolving one hierarchical authorization decision, and enforcing it across runtime and administrative command paths.
workflows.goal: Ensure project-local effects execute or mutate state only after one consistently resolved authorization decision, while passive context remains available and headless ambiguity fails closed.
when_to_use: A tool discovers project-local configuration, packages, plugins, scripts, skills, prompts, themes, or similar resources that can execute code or change runtime behavior.
Multiple entry points such as the main runtime, package commands, and configuration commands must share the same project authorization semantics.
Authorization may be supplied by explicit overrides, extension hooks, persisted directory policy, global defaults, or an interactive user decision.
anti_goals: Do not execute project-local hooks or install project packages to determine whether that same project is trusted.
Do not treat passive instruction files as equivalent to executable or configuration-driven effects unless repository evidence establishes that they execute effects.
Do not let a permissive default override an explicit persisted denial.
Do not silently authorize unresolved effect-bearing projects merely because the caller is non-interactive.
Do not require exact-directory duplication when an explicit parent-scope authorization is intended.
not_applicable_when: The project exposes no local input capable of executing code, installing dependencies, mutating configuration, or injecting runtime resources.
The caller has no project-local resource loading or mutation boundary to protect.
Authorization must not be inherited across directory ancestry for the target security model.
inputs: Canonical working directory and its ancestor chain
Inventory of passive context and effect-bearing project inputs
Explicit per-invocation authorization override, if present
Non-project policy-hook sources and hook result, if any
Resource loaders and project-local mutation operations to gate
workflows.entry_state: Project trust is unresolved; project-local effect-bearing resources and settings must be considered unavailable, while non-project configuration is readable.
workflows.exit_state: Exactly one authorization result has been installed before effect-bearing resolution: denied projects cannot load or mutate gated project state, authorized projects can be reloaded normally, passive context follows its separate classification, and any remembered scope is queryable with its source path.

steps.condition: Always, before deciding whether authorization is required.
steps.validation: The trust-input predicate is false for passive instruction files alone and true for the configured effect-bearing project markers.

steps.condition: Run only when no explicit override was supplied, gated inputs exist, and non-project policy hooks are supported.
steps.validation: Bootstrap settings report untrusted state and the loaded hook set excludes project-local packages and extensions.

steps.condition: Use when consulting or updating persisted authorization state.
steps.validation: Lookup returns the closest ancestor entry and deletion of a child entry restores the parent's effective decision.

steps.condition: Always when effect-bearing trust inputs exist; consume the bootstrap hook result when that optional step ran.
steps.validation: Precedence is override, hook, nearest persisted decision, global default, interactive decision, then denial; a stored false decision beats a global always default.

steps.condition: Before resolving project packages/resources or mutating project-local settings.
steps.validation: Denied execution exposes no gated project resources or install effects and refuses local writes; authorized execution reloads and exposes configured project resources.

validation_ladder: Unit-test the trust-input classifier, including passive-only and effect-bearing fixtures.
Unit-test hierarchical storage with parent inheritance, closer overrides, override deletion, malformed-store preservation, and source-path reporting.
Unit-test global default parsing and confirm project-local settings cannot set the default policy.
Integration-test decision precedence through package or resource call sites, including hook authorization and persisted denial over a permissive default.
Integration-test resource isolation so denied projects cannot supply executable/configuration resources while separately classified passive context remains available.
Spawn a non-interactive command and verify unresolved trust produces no project package-install side effects or structured-output contamination.
stop_conditions: Stop and deny project effects if trust remains unresolved and no interactive UI is available.
Stop and surface an error if the persisted trust store is malformed; do not overwrite it with a guessed decision.
Stop before project-local package installation, extension execution, or settings mutation if the resolved decision is false.
Defer hierarchical authorization if canonical ancestry or the intended inheritance boundary cannot be established safely.
unresolved_or_deferred: The available bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, or status-check results, so design intent beyond code, tests, and commit metadata is unavailable.
No test command was executed during this extraction; validation claims describe the checked-in test oracles at the pinned commit.

The change deliberately leaves passive project instructions outside the trust gate; whether instruction content itself should be treated as an effect in other systems is a project-specific policy decision, not established universally by this episode.

workflows.name: honor-server-retry-deadlines-across-layered-recovery
workflows.title: Honor server retry deadlines across layered recovery
workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for systems where retry advice crosses transport, semantic-error, provider, and streaming boundaries before the next attempt is scheduled.
workflows.goal: Make every eligible retry honor the server's originally requested earliest retry time without restarting the countdown during error propagation and without replacing established retry policy when advice is unavailable.
when_to_use: A client receives retry timing from HTTP headers or streamed errors but currently retries using only local backoff.
Retry advice passes through multiple error mappings, notifications, provider adapters, or exhausted-retry state before reuse.
Observed retry waits begin too late because each layer stores or reconstructs a relative duration.
anti_goals: Do not make terminal failures retryable merely because they carry retry advice.
Do not expand configured retry budgets or remove existing transport-fallback and unbounded connection-retry policies.
Do not replace local backoff for failures with missing or invalid server advice.
Do not treat an expired valid deadline as missing advice and introduce a new backoff delay.
