not_applicable_when: The upstream protocol supplies no retry timing and local backoff is already the intended complete policy.
The operation is not safely retryable or retry eligibility cannot be established independently of timing advice.
Retry timing never crosses an asynchronous or abstraction boundary and an existing absolute-deadline representation is already preserved end to end.
inputs: Raw server retry-advice headers or streamed delay signal
Clock facilities supporting a monotonic deadline
Transport and semantic error types crossed by the failure
Retry eligibility rules and configured retry budgets
Request and stream retry call sites
Deterministic clock-controlled and end-to-end recovery tests
workflows.entry_state: Retryable failures may contain server advice, but request retries ignore it or higher layers carry relative durations that can restart during propagation.
workflows.exit_state: Valid advice is captured once, preserved unchanged across all relevant error boundaries, and consumed as an absolute deadline by eligible retry schedulers; invalid or absent advice uses local backoff, while zero or expired valid advice produces an immediate eligible retry rather than fallback delay.

steps.condition: Required when the failure source can provide server retry timing.
steps.validation: Parser and transport tests establish accepted formats, receipt-time capture, countdown, expiry, and invalid-value behavior.

steps.condition: Required for every error translation, reclassification, provider rewrite, or exhausted-retry record between receipt and scheduling.
steps.validation: Mapping tests assert the same deadline survives translation and its remaining delay continues to decrease through elapsed virtual time.

steps.condition: Required only after existing policy independently declares the failure retryable and budget remains; use local backoff when no valid deadline exists.
steps.validation: Virtual-time and end-to-end tests prove sleep-until behavior, delayed-notification accounting, local-backoff fallback, bounded attempts, telemetry, and successful recovery.

validation_ladder: Unit-test parsing of delta-seconds, HTTP dates, explicit zero, expired dates, malformed values, and overflow.
Test transport capture before body processing and verify advice is attached to unsuccessful-response errors.
Test each error-mapping boundary for deadline identity and decreasing remaining duration.
Use paused time to prove intervening notification or propagation work consumes the original wait rather than preceding a fresh delay.
Verify no-advice failures still use bounded jittered backoff and retry eligibility remains independent of advice.
Run end-to-end recovery with a mock server, retry telemetry, elapsed-time assertion, successful completion, and exact request count.
Exercise retry exhaustion and confirm the last captured deadline remains available and becomes zero rather than absent after expiry.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the response-arrival boundary cannot be identified reliably enough to capture advice once.
Stop if retryability or idempotency is unresolved; timing advice alone must not authorize another attempt.
Stop if an error-mapping boundary drops metadata and cannot be changed or tested without altering a public compatibility contract.
Stop when retry budget is exhausted or the existing policy classifies the error as terminal, while retaining advice only if downstream recovery state explicitly requires it.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation leaves a TODO for honoring server advice before switching from WebSockets to fallback HTTP transport.
The buffered execute path notes that retry advice is not preserved when unbounded diagnostic-body reading itself fails with a network or timeout classification.
Wrapped WebSocket HTTP errors introduced in this change still populate retry_after as None rather than parsing their available headers.

workflows.name: repair-model-alias-budget-resolution
workflows.title: Repair context and output budgeting for a supported model alias
workflows.description: A bounded workflow for correcting an official model name that falls through ordered capability tables and destabilizes long-session compaction, while preserving existing family fallbacks.
workflows.goal: Ensure a supported official model identifier initializes configuration with its actual input-context and output-generation budgets instead of generic defaults, without changing unrelated model-family behavior.
when_to_use: A supported model alias is accepted by the endpoint but resolves to a generic or default token limit.
Long sessions or compaction fail because the configured context or output budget is lower than the model capability associated with an equivalent versioned name.
Input and output capabilities are maintained in separate ordered classifiers that can drift or fall through independently.
anti_goals: Do not globally raise default context or output limits to accommodate one alias.
Do not reorder or broaden generic family rules in a way that upgrades older models without evidence.
Do not change the compaction algorithm when the demonstrated defect is capability classification.
Do not accept endpoint-incompatible spellings as a substitute for recognizing the endpoint's official identifier.
not_applicable_when: The model identifier is not supported by the target endpoint.
The authoritative model capability is unknown or disputed.
The failure persists when configuration already contains the correct input and output budgets.
The repository does not derive runtime context or output budgets from model-name classification.
inputs: The ordered input and output classifier tables
Representative specific-family and generic-family regression examples
workflows.entry_state: The endpoint-accepted alias misses at least one specific capability classifier and receives a generic or default budget inconsistent with its intended model tier.
workflows.exit_state: The alias resolves to the intended input and output budgets through specific rules ordered before broader fallbacks, and committed regression assertions cover both dimensions plus unaffected family behavior.

steps.condition: Apply when direct inspection proves that the official identifier falls through one or both ordered capability tables.
steps.validation: Static inspection shows the alias is covered by the specific rule before the generic family rule in both input and output classifiers.

steps.condition: Run after both classifier mappings express the intended capability contract.
steps.validation: The focused oracle asserts the exact input and output values, while adjacent family assertions constrain unintended widening.

validation_ladder: Inspect the pre-change ordered classifiers and calculate which specific, generic, or default branches the alias selects.
Inspect the post-change classifiers to confirm both input and output dimensions recognize the alias before broader fallbacks.
Run or evaluate the focused unit assertions for the alias's exact input and output limits.
Run neighboring family assertions to detect unintended classifier widening.
If the checkout is executable, run the package's focused token-limit test target; otherwise record execution as deferred rather than claiming a pass.
stop_conditions: Stop if no authoritative input and output limits can be established for the alias.
Stop if the identifier is rejected by the endpoint; classification changes cannot repair endpoint incompatibility.
Stop and investigate another layer if the alias already resolves to the correct limits.
Do not claim runtime validation when the committed test cannot be executed in the supplied checkout.

workflows.name: broaden-approved-effects-with-explicit-denial-isolation
workflows.title: Broaden approved filesystem effects while preserving denial boundaries
workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for granting broad write effects to an approved command without inheriting unrelated grants or allowing mount translation, devices, aliases, or metadata symlinks to weaken explicit read denials.
workflows.goal: Run an approved command with broad filesystem write authority while preserving every enforceable explicit read denial and making the platform guarantee discoverable to clients.
when_to_use: An approval transition must broaden a restricted command from scoped writes to filesystem-root or volume-root writes.
The sandbox represents explicit denied paths or globs that must survive the approval transition.
The platform implements broad access through bind mounts, volume expansion, or comparable remapping that can shadow devices or reopen aliased targets.
anti_goals: Do not retain unrelated read or write grants from the pre-approval policy.
Do not silently drop, weaken, or reinterpret an explicit denial to make broad approval succeed.
Do not bind aliases or protected metadata paths redundantly when doing so can undo an already-applied denial mask.
Do not advertise a safety guarantee on platforms or executors that do not implement it.
not_applicable_when: Approval does not broaden filesystem effects.
The policy has no restricted-mode transformation or no explicit denial semantics to preserve.
The execution backend does not remap roots, volumes, aliases, or device trees and cannot exhibit the documented reopening or shadowing failure modes.
Required denials are intentionally revoked by a separately authorized policy decision rather than preserved through approval.
workflows.entry_state: The command's current policy limits writes and may explicitly deny reads; approval requires broader writes, but no safe broadened policy or advertised execution guarantee has yet been established.
workflows.exit_state: The approved command can perform intended broad writes and use required standard devices, explicit denials remain effective through aliases and metadata symlinks, unsafe transformations fall back instead of widening access, and compatible clients can detect the implemented guarantee.

steps.condition: Run when approval requires broader filesystem writes under a restricted policy.
steps.validation: Policy-level tests prove retained path and glob denials, removed unrelated grants, allowed root and metadata writes, cross-platform root materialization, and unchanged-policy fallback for unsafe inputs.

steps.condition: Run for a backend whose root, volume, alias, metadata, or device remapping can change the effective policy.
steps.validation: Mount-plan and integration tests prove device restoration occurs after the root bind and before explicit masks, aliases do not rebind the root, metadata symlinks cannot reopen denied targets, and explicit carveouts behave narrowly.

steps.condition: Run when clients or remote peers choose behavior based on executor support.
steps.validation: Wire tests prove default omission, false-on-absence compatibility, independent partial support, full round-trip behavior, and platform-correct local advertisement.

validation_ladder: Policy transformation: assert exact approved entries, resolved access, deny matching, removal of prior grants, and fail-closed fallback.
Platform projection: assert writable roots, protected-metadata handling, literal denial retention, volume expansion, alias suppression, and mount ordering.
Sandbox integration: execute device reads, allowed writes, denied reads, metadata-symlink attempts, writable-symlink crossings, and narrow nested carveouts.
Protocol compatibility: verify absent, partial, and full capability serialization and platform-specific advertisement.
Run the relevant Rust unit and Linux integration test targets in an environment with bubblewrap/user-namespace support; the bundle does not provide an execution result.
stop_conditions: Stop and keep the original policy if a workspace-relative denial lacks workspace roots, denial materialization or matching fails, the filesystem root cannot be identified, or the root is explicitly denied.
Stop promotion if broad root writes can shadow required devices or any alias or metadata mount can reopen a denied target.
Stop capability advertisement unless the corresponding device and denial-preservation behaviors are implemented and validated.
Defer execution-level confirmation when the host cannot run bubblewrap or create the required user namespace.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle has no CI status, review record, or recorded test-run result; validation is grounded in added test oracles rather than observed execution.
The pinned change introduces and directly tests approved-policy derivation, but the inspected evidence does not establish a non-test production caller that invokes the new transformation.
Client-side consumption of the two new capability fields is outside this commit and remains deferred.

workflows.name: resume-persisted-conversation-safely
workflows.title: Resume a persisted conversation without displacing live state or overflowing context
workflows.description: A partial-order startup workflow that reconstructs a persisted transcript only when authoritative live state is absent, then conditionally compacts oversized restored state under both session and model context limits.
workflows.goal: Start a session with usable prior conversational context while preserving explicit caller state and keeping restored history within configured and model-imposed token limits.
when_to_use: A stateful interactive application persists a transcript across process lifetimes and a new session should continue the prior conversation.
The persisted representation contains both conversational content and operational metadata that must not be replayed as model dialogue.
Restored state can be large enough to require compaction before continued use.
anti_goals: Do not replace explicitly supplied in-memory conversation state with disk contents.
Do not replay tool output, session metadata, commands, or blank prompts as conversational messages.
Do not summarize history that already fits the configured retained-history budget.
Do not send an unbounded restored transcript to the summarizer model.
not_applicable_when: The application has no persisted conversation artifact to resume.
The persisted artifact cannot be deterministically mapped to ordered conversational roles.
A caller requires explicit supplied state and persisted state to be merged rather than using explicit state as authoritative.
No reliable token counter or summarizer input limit is available for safe compaction.
inputs: history token budget or model default
workflows.entry_state: Session initialization has begun; completed-message state is either explicitly supplied or empty, and a configured transcript may contain earlier conversation plus operational records.
workflows.exit_state: Explicit completed-message state has been preserved, or persisted conversational messages have been restored; any restored state exceeding its budget has entered bounded compaction, and nonempty restored state is visible through the startup announcement.

steps.condition: Run when completed-message state is empty and the configured transcript contains text.
steps.validation: Verify ordered user/assistant reconstruction and exclusion of recognized metadata, tool output, commands, and blank prompts.

steps.condition: Always enforce precedence; file loading and reconstruction are conditional on the absence of explicit completed-message state.
steps.validation: Verify explicit state is unchanged, while empty state with a populated transcript becomes restored state and produces the restoration announcement.

steps.condition: Evaluate every restored state; start compaction only when its token count exceeds the selected history budget.
steps.validation: Verify threshold behavior and confirm that any summarizer request is restricted to content fitting within the summarizer input limit minus its reserve.

validation_ladder: Unit-check transcript reconstruction with representative user, assistant, session-heading, blockquote, command, and blank-prompt records.
Lifecycle-check precedence using both explicit completed messages and an empty state backed by a populated transcript.
Boundary-check compaction immediately below and above the configured history-token threshold.
Capacity-check that a large selected head is trimmed to the summarizer model's input capacity minus the reserved tokens.
Integration-check that a restarted session reports restoration and can continue using the restored completed-message state.
stop_conditions: Stop restoration and retain explicit state when completed messages were supplied by the caller.
Stop file-based restoration when the configured transcript is absent, unreadable through the input adapter, or empty.
Stop promotion as a fully validated resolution until automated parser, precedence, and compaction tests exist.
Stop or repair if transcript reconstruction cannot preserve conversational ordering or if bounded summarization fails.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned change includes no automated tests for transcript parsing, state precedence, startup restoration, token override propagation, or bounded compaction.
The parser does not flush a final accumulated assistant segment at end-of-file, so preservation of a transcript ending directly in assistant content is unresolved.
The standalone aider/history.py entry point calls an undefined summarize_chat_history_markdown method at the pinned ref and therefore is not a usable validation path.

The changed compaction calculation reverses and truncates the sized head before later slicing it with split_index; the exact tail-token accounting should be covered by focused boundary tests before treating it as a proven invariant.

workflows.name: enable_safe_ambient_credential_resolution
workflows.title: Enable ambient credentials without weakening credential precedence
workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for adding a keyless ambient authentication path across validation, client construction, diagnostics, and status reporting while preventing silent principal changes.
workflows.goal: Allow a supported provider mode to resolve ambient default credentials from a project-scoped configuration while preserving explicit secret precedence, correct endpoint routing, truthful status, and actionable failures.
when_to_use: A provider SDK supports ambient or application-default credentials, but application validation currently requires an explicit API key.
Passing a placeholder credential changes SDK mode or disables the intended ambient credential resolver.
The same authentication decision is enforced at multiple startup or configuration boundaries.
anti_goals: Do not fabricate, inject, or pass a placeholder API key to satisfy validation.
Do not silently fall back to ambient credentials when the selected provider entry declares a specific key source.
Do not infer the selected authentication mode from project configuration alone when explicit mode selection is required.
Do not report a configured project as proof that a usable credential has resolved.
Do not broaden the keyless path to unrelated authentication modes.
not_applicable_when: The provider SDK does not support ambient credential resolution.
No routing context required by the ambient resolver is configured.
The selected provider entry explicitly requires a key source that must remain authoritative.
The authentication mode cannot be selected independently of credential presence.
inputs: resolved API key and its source
project or routing identifier from process and settings
startup validation and preflight entry points
workflows.entry_state: The intended provider mode is selected and ambient credentials may exist, but missing-key checks prevent startup or a placeholder key changes SDK behavior; validation, construction, and status surfaces may disagree.
workflows.exit_state: Eligible project-only configurations pass every startup validation gate, construct the SDK client in the intended mode with no key, preserve explicit secret contracts, provide applicable recovery guidance, and leave actual ambient credential resolution unconfirmed until session startup.

steps.condition: Always establish the exact boundary before relaxing any missing-key check.
steps.validation: Boundary tests distinguish nonblank routing context from blank or whitespace values and exclude unrelated auth modes and declared key sources.

steps.condition: Apply whenever configurations may declare their own credential source.
steps.validation: An unset declared key remains an error even when ambient routing context is present.

steps.condition: Apply to every gate that can reject the resolved authentication configuration before client use.
steps.validation: CLI and core validators agree on eligible, ineligible, strict, and explicit-key configurations.

steps.condition: Apply when the SDK's endpoint or authentication behavior depends on mode flags or key presence.
steps.validation: The constructed client receives the intended mode flag and no API key without relying on a prior environment mutation.

steps.condition: Apply to missing-credential errors exposed by the affected validation gates.
steps.validation: The ambient-credential hint appears only where the classifier says the path is applicable.

steps.condition: Apply when a preflight or status surface reports token availability before the SDK attempts ambient resolution.
steps.validation: Eligible project-only status is indeterminate rather than authenticated or missing-key failed.

validation_ladder: Predicate-level cases: nonblank, absent, and whitespace-only routing identifiers.
Precedence cases: declared key source remains mandatory despite available ambient context.
Cross-gate cases: CLI and core validators accept and reject the same configurations, including strict mode.
Construction case: selected mode reaches the SDK explicitly and the key remains undefined.
Diagnostic cases: recovery guidance is present only for eligible failures.
Status case: routing readiness is reported as unknown credential availability.
Runtime follow-up: start a session in an environment with valid ambient credentials and separately verify failure with unavailable ambient credentials.
stop_conditions: Stop if project or routing configuration cannot be distinguished from proof of credential availability.
Stop if a declared credential source would be bypassed or the authenticated principal could change silently.
Stop if any startup validator still rejects an otherwise eligible configuration.
Stop if client construction sends any placeholder key or selects the wrong endpoint mode.
Stop if tests cannot demonstrate exclusion of unrelated auth types and explicit-key configurations.

workflows.name: preserve-caller-state-during-resume
workflows.title: Resume from history without corrupting caller-owned state
workflows.description: Establish an ownership boundary for a mutable history passed into a continuation routine, extend only a copied working sequence, and validate both preservation of the input and growth of the returned state.
workflows.goal: Continue an operation from existing history while returning the newly extended history and preserving the caller's original history container.
when_to_use: A continuation or resume API accepts a caller-supplied mutable sequence and appends new state during processing.
Inspection or regression behavior shows that the routine aliases and mutates the caller's non-empty sequence.
anti_goals: Do not remove prior history from the working continuation state.
Do not suppress recording of the new user or assistant messages in the returned state.
Do not deep-copy or transform individual history entries unless nested-entry mutation is separately demonstrated and specified.
not_applicable_when: The API explicitly documents in-place mutation as part of its contract.
The supplied history is immutable or the routine never mutates the sequence structure.
The defect concerns mutation of nested message objects rather than append operations on the outer sequence.
inputs: continuation entry point that accepts prior history
deterministic completion or equivalent response fixture
workflows.entry_state: A non-empty caller-owned history can be bound directly to the routine's working sequence, and later append operations can therefore corrupt the caller's preserved state.
workflows.exit_state: The routine operates on a distinct outer sequence, preserves all supplied history entries for continuation, appends the new turn to the working result, and leaves the caller's input sequence structurally unchanged.

steps.condition: Apply when the continuation routine performs structural mutations such as append on a caller-supplied mutable sequence.
steps.validation: Inspect the initialization boundary and confirm that supplied history is copied into a distinct working sequence before any new-turn append occurs.

steps.condition: Run after the ownership boundary is changed and a deterministic completed-turn fixture is available.
steps.validation: Confirm that the caller's sequence length equals its pre-call baseline and that the returned sequence length exceeds that baseline.

validation_ladder: Static boundary check: the working outer sequence is constructed separately from a supplied mutable history.
Behavioral preservation check: after a completed new turn, the caller's history retains its original length.
Behavioral continuity check: the returned history is longer than the original, proving that isolation did not discard the new turn.
Focused automated regression test when the test runner and dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the API contract intentionally transfers ownership and permits in-place mutation.
Stop and broaden the investigation if individual pre-existing message objects are mutated, because a shallow sequence copy does not isolate nested objects.
Defer runtime confirmation if the repository's test runner or required dependencies are unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed test checks outer-list length, not object identity, exact preserved contents, or mutation of nested message dictionaries.
A fresh test execution is deferred because pytest is not installed in the supplied environment.

workflows.name: align-resume-interface-with-persisted-runtime-route
workflows.title: Align a resume interface with the authoritative persisted runtime route
workflows.description: Resolve cross-interface resume failures by identifying the metadata actually updated by the producer, defining a single precedence contract for legacy and current representations, and routing the inconsistent consumer through that contract while preserving its local safety behavior.
workflows.goal: A session resumed through any supported interface uses the provider, endpoint, and protocol associated with its latest persisted runtime execution rather than combining its model with stale route metadata.
when_to_use: A producer and one resume consumer use a nested or versioned runtime snapshot while another consumer reconstructs the same route from older top-level or accounting fields.
A resumed model is sent to the wrong provider endpoint or protocol after the session changes providers.
Multiple consumers interpret the same persisted route with different precedence rules.
anti_goals: Do not change provider selection for new sessions that have no usable persisted route.
Do not treat accounting buckets as authoritative route identities when they are documented as frozen or non-routable.
Do not remove interface-specific endpoint-ownership checks, stale-provider healing, reasoning settings, service-tier handling, or profile-following behavior.
Do not persist or restore raw API credentials as part of route reconciliation.
not_applicable_when: There is no durable runtime-route representation or no evidence identifying which representation is freshest.
The failure occurs during initial provider discovery rather than restoration of an existing session.
The differing consumers intentionally implement distinct routing semantics rather than alternate interfaces to the same resumed session.
inputs: Persisted session-row shapes from every writer
All resume consumers of the stored route
Documented route-field precedence and non-routable fallback values
Regression tests representing stale and current metadata combinations
workflows.entry_state: At least one resume interface can read a stale provider, endpoint, or API mode because its local metadata interpretation differs from the writer and from another resume consumer.
workflows.exit_state: All examined resume interfaces consume the same canonical route precedence, the latest nested route wins over stale representations, partial legacy metadata remains compatible, and unsafe fallback identities remain filtered.

steps.condition: The persisted row has multiple current or legacy route representations whose precedence and fallback composition must be made explicit.
steps.validation: Canonical-reader tests prove nested precedence, legacy top-level support, routable fallback completion, bare-bucket rejection, and malformed-input tolerance.

steps.condition: A resume consumer independently decodes route metadata instead of using the established canonical resolver.
steps.validation: Cross-interface regression tests prove the adapted consumer and the existing canonical consumer select the nested current route over stale billing and top-level values.

validation_ladder: Inspect the writer to confirm which persisted representation is refreshed on each executed turn.
Unit-test the canonical resolver across nested, top-level, partial, malformed, routable-fallback, and non-routable-fallback inputs.
Run consumer-level regression tests with a stale first-call billing provider and a newer nested route.
Run consumer-level regression tests with stale top-level endpoint/protocol keys and a newer nested route.
Run existing resume compatibility tests for endpoint ownership, provider healing, legacy rows, profile-following exclusions, reasoning configuration, and service tier.
Run repository diff validation and the focused test module in the supported project environment.
stop_conditions: Stop if the producer's authoritative or freshest representation cannot be established from code or tests.
Stop if the proposed canonical precedence would discard a supported legacy route representation without a migration or compatibility oracle.
Stop if the consumer has intentionally different routing semantics and therefore should not share the resolver.
Do not claim runtime validation complete unless the focused tests execute successfully in a dependency-complete environment.

workflows.name: recover-consecutive-no-answer-response-stall
workflows.title: Recover a turn stuck producing internal reasoning without an answer
workflows.description: Detect consecutive incomplete responses with no user-visible progress, escalate the live turn through the configured fallback chain with a strictly bounded budget exception, and adapt the transcript if the fallback speaks a different request protocol.
workflows.goal: Complete the same user turn through a configured fallback when repeated incomplete responses contain neither an answer nor a tool call, without allowing unbounded retries or leaking source-protocol control state.
when_to_use: A response API repeatedly returns an incomplete status while exposing no visible answer text and no tool call.
The runtime has an existing fallback chain capable of continuing the same turn.
Continuation replay or a synthetic nudge has already failed to produce observable progress.
anti_goals: Do not classify visible partial progress as part of an uninterrupted no-answer streak.
Do not grant an open-ended iteration-budget extension or repeatedly allocate grace calls.
Do not mutate canonical conversation history solely to satisfy the fallback protocol.
Do not send source-protocol continuation markers or opaque replay state to an incompatible destination.
Do not replace the existing terminal partial-result behavior when no fallback can be activated.
not_applicable_when: The response contains visible answer content or a tool call and therefore demonstrates progress.
The failure is a transport exception, policy refusal, malformed request, or another condition already represented by a different recovery reason.
No fallback is configured or permitted and the caller requires immediate terminal handling.
The destination uses the same protocol and can safely consume the existing replay and continuation state.
inputs: Normalized response status, visible content, and tool-call fields
Per-turn consecutive-stall and aggregate incomplete counters
Configured fallback chain and typed recovery reason
API call count and remaining iteration budget
Current request protocol and fallback request protocol
Canonical session messages and active system identity
workflows.entry_state: A live turn has received an incomplete response; continuation state and aggregate retry accounting exist, but the runtime must determine whether this response extends a consecutive no-answer stall.
workflows.exit_state: Either a configured fallback has received a protocol-compatible request and produced a normal turn result using no more than one bounded grace call, or fallback activation was unavailable and the established terminal partial-result path handled the turn.

steps.condition: For every incomplete response in the active turn.
steps.validation: The streak increments only when both visible content and tool calls are absent, and resets on visible progress or a normal response.

steps.condition: The consecutive-stall threshold is reached and the configured fallback chain can activate; otherwise retain terminal partial handling.
steps.validation: The fallback receives incomplete_response, the same turn continues, and an exhausted normal budget yields exactly one additional request opportunity.

steps.condition: Fallback activation changes to a protocol that must not receive the source protocol's continuation marker or opaque reasoning replay state.
steps.validation: The fallback wire excludes incompatible recovery artifacts and retains valid role alternation, while stored session history remains intact.

validation_ladder: Unit-level state oracle: visible progress resets the local stall streak independently of aggregate incomplete-response accounting.
Recovery integration oracle: three consecutive no-answer responses invoke the typed fallback reason and produce the fallback's completed answer.
Budget oracle: a stall that consumes the normal three-call budget produces exactly one fallback grace call and leaves the grace flag consumed.
Protocol-handoff oracle: the fallback wire contains neither source-only continuation text nor opaque reasoning replay state and preserves alternating non-system roles.

Regression oracle: when fallback activation fails, terminal partial-result behavior remains available; this branch is supported by implementation inspection but has no new focused test in the changed test file.
stop_conditions: Stop retrying through this workflow once a normal response supplies visible content or a tool call.
Stop after the fallback consumes the single grace request; do not allocate another grace call for the same stall.
Stop escalation and use the existing terminal partial result when no fallback can be activated.
Defer promotion if the runtime cannot reliably distinguish visible output and tool calls or lacks a configured fallback mechanism.

workflows.name: harden_context_summary_generation
workflows.title: Harden context-summary generation against transient request failures
workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for adding bounded, abortable retry behavior to context-compaction and branch-summary requests while preserving deterministic failure behavior, supplied-summary bypasses, and observable operation state.
workflows.goal: Generated context summaries recover from temporary provider or transport failures within a configured budget without masking terminal failures or making operation state opaque.
when_to_use: A context compaction, truncation, checkpoint, or branch-preservation operation depends on a model-generated summary.
A transient stream or transport failure currently aborts the entire structural context operation on its first failed request.
The runtime already has, or can accept, a bounded retry policy and an operation cancellation signal.
anti_goals: Do not retry context-overflow, quota, billing, authentication, or other errors rejected by the transient-error classifier.
Do not create an unbounded retry loop or silently ignore the configured retry budget.
Do not retry summaries supplied by hooks, extensions, caches, or callers when no model request is made.
Do not change summary selection, token budgeting, retained-tail boundaries, prompts, or persistence semantics merely to add request resilience.
not_applicable_when: The failure is caused by deterministic summary preparation, invalid session structure, or an unusable context boundary rather than a transient assistant request error.
The operation has no model-generated summary request.
The system cannot classify failed assistant responses or cannot cancel a pending retry delay safely.
inputs: Retry policy with enabled, maxRetries, and baseDelayMs
Cancellation signal scoped to the structural operation
Scripted completion responses for success, transient failure, terminal failure, and abort
workflows.entry_state: Context-summary preparation succeeds, but at least one generated summary path performs a single request whose transient failure terminates compaction or branch preservation.
workflows.exit_state: All generated summary paths use the same bounded retry invariant, retain existing operation cancellation and supplied-summary behavior, expose retry lifecycle state, and satisfy recovery and terminal-case regression oracles.

steps.condition: A failed assistant response can be classified as transient or terminal and the caller can provide a retry policy.
steps.validation: Utility-level scripted responses prove bounded attempts, exponential-delay callbacks, fail-fast exclusions, successful recovery, and abortable backoff.

steps.condition: Execute only for model-generated summaries; bypass when a hook or extension already supplied the summary.
steps.validation: Entry-point tests prove compaction and branch-summary recovery after transient failures and unchanged failure behavior when retry is disabled, exhausted, aborted, or terminal.

steps.condition: The host exposes operation events or interactive status and retry delays are externally observable.
steps.validation: Subscriber tests verify operation-tagged scheduled/start/finished order; UI handlers restore the underlying compaction or branch-summary status and clear retry state on completion.

validation_ladder: Unit-test the retry primitive with immediate success, abort, terminal error, disabled policy, recovery, exhaustion, callback order, and cancellation during backoff.
Test each orchestration family with scripted assistant responses: context compaction and branch preservation must recover after transient failures and stop at the configured budget.
Run the issue regression scenario using a transient mid-stream "terminated" response and assert the summary is persisted only after recovery.
Verify observability: lifecycle events carry attempt counts, delays, errors, and operation context, while terminal errors emit no retry lifecycle.
Run the repository's required static check and the specific modified test files before considering the change complete.
stop_conditions: Stop and fail fast when the response is aborted or the classifier rejects the error as non-retryable.
Stop after maxRetries retry attempts and return the final error.
Stop retry waiting immediately when the operation abort signal fires.
Defer implementation if no stable summary-request boundary can receive both retry policy and cancellation signal.
Do not claim completion if any generated summary call site still bypasses the retry boundary unintentionally.

workflows.name: restore-explicit-credential-source-precedence
workflows.title: Restore deliberate credential selection without breaking ambient fallback
workflows.description: Trace the provenance of a selected profile into the runtime client, preserve that provenance as an authoritative marker, and use it to prevent lower-priority ambient keys from becoming explicit client credentials. Validate both the repaired conflict and unaffected fallback cases.
workflows.goal: Ensure a deliberately selected credential profile controls authentication when ambient access keys coexist, while retaining ambient credential behavior when no deliberate profile selection exists.
when_to_use: A client configuration can contain both a profile selector and directly injected credentials, and the SDK gives the direct credentials higher precedence.
Authentication resolution carries a request-explicit or stored/scoped profile into the provider runtime while ambient access keys may also be visible.
anti_goals: Do not disable ambient access-key authentication when no authoritative profile was selected.
Do not treat a merely ambient profile as equivalent to a request-explicit or stored/scoped selection.
Do not alter bearer-token selection, skip-auth dummy credentials, region selection, endpoint selection, or proxy behavior.
not_applicable_when: Credential sources cannot coexist or the downstream client does not give directly supplied credentials precedence over profile-based resolution.
The failure concerns bearer-token authentication, disabled signing, incomplete access-key pairs, or credential-store persistence rather than profile-versus-key precedence.
There is no evidence that the selected profile reaches the provider request options.
inputs: Provider-resolved scoped environment, including any stored profile
Ambient profile and access-key environment values
workflows.entry_state: A deliberate profile can reach the runtime, but a complete ambient access-key pair is independently injected as explicit credentials and can override that profile.
workflows.exit_state: Explicit or stored/scoped profiles suppress lower-priority direct access-key injection; access keys remain injected when no authoritative profile exists, including when the profile value is only ambient.

steps.condition: Apply when profile values may originate from request-explicit, stored/scoped, or ambient sources.
steps.validation: Confirm that explicit options and scoped request environment produce the authoritative marker, while ambient lookup remains only a fallback for the client profile field.

workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for detecting repeated tool requests that differ textually but share one non-progressing semantic operation, while preserving productive variants and propagating a structured halt contract.
workflows.goal: Halt a bounded run of semantically equivalent, non-progressing tool requests even when their raw arguments vary, without stopping productive or targeted operations.
when_to_use: A tool loop evades exact request equality because the model rewrites arguments while repeating the same observable read-only operation.
The repeated operation has a narrow semantic class with evidence-backed exclusions precise enough for an always-on or high-confidence guard.
The runtime already has a termination path capable of discarding queued calls and emitting a structured reason.
anti_goals: Do not classify all repeated uses of one tool name as equivalent.
Do not stop write-bearing, mixed-purpose, targeted-review, or otherwise progress-bearing operations merely because they contain an inspection segment.
Do not place the new precise guard behind a broad heuristic-skip setting when the intended contract is always-on, though an explicit session-level disable may remain honored.
Do not alter unrelated content, thought, read-file, alternating-call, or hard-cap detectors.
not_applicable_when: No stable semantic equivalence class can be derived from the structured request or command payload.
The suspected loop includes productive state changes or target-specific narrowing that constitutes progress.
Only issue-title or similarity evidence exists without an implementation diff and validation oracle.
The consumer has no safe halt path for cancelling queued operations and reporting the reason.
inputs: Counterexamples that must count as progress
Structured tool name and argument payload
Retry, prompt-reset, and session-disable lifecycle semantics
Typed loop-event, telemetry, and user-message contracts
workflows.entry_state: Exact request equality does not catch a repeated semantic operation because each consecutive request varies its arguments, so the run can continue until a distant generic cap or external failure.
workflows.exit_state: Only the proven non-progressing request class shares a semantic key; its uninterrupted streak halts at the configured bound, progress and replay boundaries reset it, excluded operations continue, and all consumers receive one structured halt reason.

steps.condition: Use only after positive loop variants and productive counterexamples establish a narrow semantic boundary.
steps.validation: Positive overview-inspection variants share one key, while write-bearing, mixed, non-repository, and path-specific cases do not.

steps.condition: Apply when consecutive requests receive the admitted semantic key and detection is not explicitly disabled for the session.
steps.validation: The threshold request fires; threshold-minus-one does not; nonmatching requests, retries, and prompt resets restart counting.

steps.condition: Apply whenever the new circuit breaker reports detection.
steps.validation: The production stream clears pending calls, emits the dedicated reason, terminates, logs telemetry, and provides a matching user-facing explanation.

validation_ladder: Classifier unit boundary: admit distinct overview-style read-only variants and reject productive, mixed-purpose, unrelated, and targeted operations.
State-machine boundary: verify threshold-minus-one, exact threshold, interruption reset, retry reset, prompt reset, and explicit session disable.
Integration boundary: confirm the guard executes before configuration-gated heuristics and clears queued requests on detection.
Contract boundary: confirm one dedicated reason is consistent across detector state, emitted stream event, telemetry, and user-facing text.
Repository validation: run the focused loop-detection test file in a clean checkout with the repository's declared runtime and package manager.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if semantic equivalence cannot be expressed narrowly enough to avoid known productive cases.
Stop if the detector cannot reset on observable progress or replay boundaries.
Stop if a firing cannot safely cancel pending requests and terminate the current run.
Do not claim runtime validation until the focused tests execute successfully in a usable checkout.

workflows.name: repair-leaking-truncated-structured-call-fragments
workflows.title: Repair leaked truncated tool-call fragments while preserving ordinary prose
workflows.description: A bounded workflow for a sanitizer that already removes malformed structured calls but misses a newly observed serialization prefix. workflows.goal: Remove unrecoverable name-prefixed structured-call fragments from assistant content at every relevant sanitization boundary without deleting natural-language mentions or later unrelated prose.

The malformed fragment is unrecoverable and should be removed rather than parsed or executed.
More than one consumer boundary is expected to enforce the same stripping contract.
anti_goals: Do not interpret, reconstruct, or execute the truncated call.
Do not accept arbitrary prose before an argument tag as a fragment prefix.
Do not remove unrelated preceding or subsequent visible prose.
Do not redesign complete structured-call parsing or unrelated reasoning-tag handling.
not_applicable_when: The input is a complete, valid structured call that should be parsed through the normal tool-call path.
The suspected prefix contains spaces or sentence text and cannot be distinguished from an inline prose example by the evidenced identifier-only rule.

Positive removal expectations and negative prose-preservation examples

workflows.name: close-multiline-policy-bypass
workflows.title: Close newline-based bypasses in a pre-execution command policy

workflows.goal: Ensure commands covered by an existing dangerous-pattern policy cannot bypass its pre-execution approval path merely by inserting newlines.

Do not alter approval scopes, prompting behavior, environment exemptions, force semantics, or command execution behavior.
Do not normalize away arbitrary whitespace or rewrite the command that will actually be executed.
not_applicable_when: The policy intentionally evaluates each line as an independent command with no cross-line constructs.
The bypass is caused by missing dangerous-operation coverage rather than newline-sensitive matching.
The matcher already spans newlines and the failure originates in parsing, canonicalization, shell semantics, or a downstream approval-state defect.

The existing dangerous-pattern catalog and matching flags
The pre-execution call path that consumes the classifier result
Representative single-line and newline-separated dangerous commands
Existing benign-command and classification regression cases

workflows.exit_state: Existing policy patterns retain their intended single-line behavior and representative covered constructs split across newlines are classified as dangerous before terminal execution.

workflows.name: preserve-selected-runtime-context-across-session-restore
workflows.title: Preserve workspace runtime context throughout session restoration

workflows.goal: Ensure every supported cold session load/resume entry point restores persisted state and invokes its bridge under the storage root owned by the selected workspace runtime.

Do not replace workspace selection logic; preserve the already selected runtime and propagate its storage context.
Do not globally mutate a process-wide storage root when a callback-scoped binding is available.
not_applicable_when: All session storage access is explicitly parameterized and no restore dependency consults ambient runtime state.
The requested session is absent from the correctly selected runtime store rather than hidden by a context mismatch.
The operation creates a new session and does not restore persisted state.
Only one immutable runtime root exists and runtime selection or replacement cannot occur.

Ambient storage-context API with asynchronous callback propagation
Tests capable of creating distinct runtime roots

workflows.exit_state: Every affected load/resume entry point scopes its complete restore critical section to the selected runtime root, and regression tests prove the selected or replacement root is visible at the bridge boundary for both actions.

branches.condition: Yes; authoritative capabilities or measurable capacity inputs identify the intended result and competing bound.
No; the capability is disputed, required usage data is unavailable, or only an ungrounded proxy could be introduced.
Input and output capabilities are maintained in separate ordered classifiers; update and validate each implicated classifier before broader fallbacks.
The provider combines a configured ceiling with current remaining capacity; select the smaller bound and validate both winner branches.

invariants: The repair occurs at the policy boundary that supplies the budget to existing consumers.
Every independent budget dimension implicated by the defect is updated and validated; correcting only one dimension is insufficient when another can still fall through.
A specific rule must take precedence over a broader fallback only when evidence supports the specific rule.
A dynamic capacity-derived bound must not weaken an existing stricter configured ceiling.
Focused checks must cover both the corrected result and at least one competing or neighboring branch.
Repository-specific classifier ordering and capacity-conversion logic remain conditional implementations, not universal mandatory steps.
validation_ladder: Focused contract checks: exercise the repaired resolver or provider with controlled inputs and assert the exact expected budget for every implicated dimension or bound.
Integration checks: verify the existing runtime configuration or guarded output path still consumes the repaired policy result without bypassing it or replacing the downstream mechanism.

Regression checks: exercise the competing precedence branch and representative neighboring identifiers, fallback rules, default configuration, or custom configuration to detect unintended widening or weakening.
Execution check: run the relevant focused test target and applicable package checks when the checkout is executable; otherwise record execution as deferred rather than claiming a pass.

known_failure_modes.failure: Only one independently resolved budget dimension is corrected.
known_failure_modes.detection: The affected input or output check passes while another capability lookup still returns a generic or default value.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Enumerate all implicated dimensions before implementation and include exact focused assertions for each one.

known_failure_modes.failure: A specific repair unintentionally changes broader fallback behavior.
known_failure_modes.detection: Representative neighboring identifiers or configurations resolve to new values despite lacking supporting evidence.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the specific rule ahead of the broad fallback and retain adjacent regression examples for unaffected behavior.

known_failure_modes.failure: A dynamic estimate overrides a stricter configured ceiling.
known_failure_modes.detection: A controlled case with a smaller configured limit returns the larger capacity-derived value.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Use the smaller applicable bound and test both precedence directions, including custom configuration.

known_failure_modes.failure: The policy is changed, but the runtime consumer bypasses it.
known_failure_modes.detection: Static call-site inspection or an integration check shows the consumer still reads a constant, stale field, or different resolver.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Trace the repaired value through the existing consumer boundary and add an integration-level assertion where supported.

known_failure_modes.failure: Tests prove only the new happy path.
known_failure_modes.detection: The suite lacks cases for the opposite precedence branch or representative unaffected fallback behavior.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Add focused branch tests and neighboring regressions before considering the repair complete.

patterns.title: Repair budget decisions at their policy boundary
patterns.summary: When an existing context-related budget resolves to an unsafe value, correct the resolver or threshold provider that owns the decision, preserve stricter constraints and unrelated fallback behavior, and add focused tests that lock the intended precedence. The exact implementation remains conditional on whether the defect is an ordered capability classification or a dynamic-versus-configured limit calculation.
when_to_use: A runtime context, generation, or retained-output budget is demonstrably lower or otherwise different from the value implied by authoritative capability or current-capacity inputs.
The incorrect value can be traced to a stable policy boundary such as an ordered capability resolver or a threshold provider.
Multiple independent limits or classifier branches can compete, and the intended winner can be expressed as an observable contract.
Downstream compaction or truncation behavior is already present and the demonstrated defect is the budget supplied to it rather than the downstream mechanism itself.
anti_goals: Do not globally raise defaults to repair one identifier, call site, or capacity condition.
Do not broaden or reorder unrelated fallback rules without evidence that their behavior should change.
Do not rewrite compaction, truncation, persistence, or file-spill mechanisms when their input budget is the defective boundary.
Do not treat approximate unit conversions as exact tokenization.
Do not validate only the newly expected value while leaving competing precedence branches and neighboring behavior unconstrained.
not_applicable_when: No authoritative capability, configured ceiling, or observable current-capacity input exists from which to derive the intended budget.
The runtime already resolves and consumes the intended budget, indicating that the failure belongs to another layer.
The affected operation does not obtain its limit through a stable resolver or threshold provider.
The failure is caused by transient request handling, summary selection, preserved-tail accounting, or another compaction contract rather than budget resolution.

action_template.title: Correct the owning budget policy
action_template.purpose: Change the existing resolver or threshold provider so the affected runtime path receives the evidence-backed budget while preserving stricter constraints and unrelated behavior.
action_template.condition: Apply after tracing the incorrect runtime value to an ordered classifier, threshold provider, or equivalent stable policy boundary.
action_template.validation: Inspect or exercise the policy boundary to confirm the affected inputs select the intended value and that the existing consumer still obtains its budget through that boundary.

action_template.title: Lock budget precedence with focused checks
action_template.purpose: Encode exact examples for the corrected budget decision, its competing precedence branch, and representative unaffected behavior.
action_template.condition: Apply after the owning budget policy expresses the intended decision for every implicated dimension.
action_template.validation: Focused tests must fail under the prior policy and pass only when the corrected value, the opposite precedence branch, and neighboring fallback or configuration behavior are all preserved.

exclusions: Bounded retry, cancellation, and retry-lifecycle observability for generated summaries are separate request-resilience contracts.
Selecting an ordered summarizer prefix and reconciling a generated summary with a preserved tail are separate compaction-accounting contracts.
